column1: # Requirements of draft-fossil-submanifests-00, written from the draft text,
# reader and writer. Skipped, with reasons, in the suite's report: 5.6 and
# 6.5 (informative), 8.2 (an operator rule for provisional repositories, not
# observable in a library) and 11 (IANA). Not implemented: the 7.4 SHOULD
# (memoized sub-manifest enumeration). The writer's construction is checked
# byte for byte against the Appendix A artifacts and against check-ins zit
# wrote (testdata/zit-writer, replayed without zit in CI).
# The draft is pinned with the 2026-10-19 errata applied: 7.2's capability
# pragma send-submanifests in place of a version threshold, avoid-submanifests
# in every reply's leading pragma run, the sync session defined (7.2, 8.1),
# configuration adopted once at clone through reqconfig /config (6.3), the
# history replay and the current check-in without a checkout (6.3), an
# invalid stored pin (8.1), and the provisional phase retired, its flag-day
# rule moved to 8.1, which the enable warning states.

A card letter outside A-Z is rejected, and the in-range undefined letters O, V, X and Y are rejected; S is defined.
An S card carries exactly a filename and a hash; a third token, or a missing hash, is rejected.
The S card filename is escape-decoded; the S card hash is never decoded.
S cards repeat, and an S run ascends strictly by decoded filename under the canonical comparator; an equal or descending neighbour is rejected.
S falls between R and T in the card order, so a manifest's S run follows its R card and precedes its T cards.
The S card hash is exactly 40 or 64 case-insensitive hexadecimal characters.
The decoded S card filename passes the pathname predicate; one that does not is rejected.
A manifest may carry an S card alongside B C D F N P Q R T U Z, and requires D and Z.
A sub-manifest may carry only F, S and Z cards, and requires a Z card.
S is a manifest-setting letter, and a manifest with no D card is reclassified as SUBMANIFEST once its type is final and before legality is checked; no card assigns SUBMANIFEST directly.
No artifact valid under the base artifact format changes classification.
A manifest carrying both a B card and an S card is rejected.
A manifest carrying both F cards and S cards is rejected.
A sub-manifest carrying both F cards and S cards, or neither, is rejected.
Every F card of a sub-manifest carries a hash; a delete marker in a sub-manifest is rejected.
The tree walk delivers each emitted F card's hash, permission and old-name tokens to consumers unaltered.
An interior sub-manifest, whose first card is S, is not rejected by a pre-filter on its first card letter.
A manifest is a tree manifest if and only if it carries an S card, and a consumer that needs its file set derives it by the tree walk.
The walk enumerates a tree depth first and in order, emitting each leaf's F cards in order, through interior sub-manifests as well as leaves.
Each S card's decoded filename, and each emitted filename, compares strictly greater than the last filename emitted; an enumeration that does not ascend across sibling slices fails.
The enumeration fails when a referenced sub-manifest is absent.
The enumeration fails when a referenced artifact is not of type SUBMANIFEST.
The enumeration fails when a referenced artifact is the artifact of a frame already on the walk's stack.
column4: a cycle cannot be built from content-addressed artifacts: the case shows the depth bound ending a path, and internal/manifest's TestTreeWalkRefusesRepeatedArtifact the check itself

column3: The enumeration fails when a sub-manifest lies deeper than 16 sub-manifests, counting the leaf; a depth of 16 is accepted.
A leaf's first emitted filename is byte-identical to the filename of the S card that reached it.
An interior sub-manifest's first S card filename is byte-identical to the filename of the S card that reached it.
Downstream consumers do not distinguish a walked enumeration from a flat one: a tree check-in's file-change records are those of a flat check-in of the same files.
The enumeration entry points, the full walk and single-name lookup, treat an unresolvable sub-manifest as a fatal error, and no partially resolved tree is presented as a complete file set.
A consumer that defers records the gap, keyed by the dependent and the missing hash and inserted idempotently, and retries when the sub-manifest arrives.
Single-name lookup binary-searches each S run for the last card at or before the name, descending one sub-manifest per level to a leaf; a name before the first S card is absent.
A lookup that would resolve a sub-manifest deeper than 16 fails, and a sub-manifest it cannot resolve fails it hard.
A delta manifest may name a tree manifest as its baseline: the merge walk takes the tree walk as its baseline cursor, and single-name lookup takes the tree lookup as its baseline step.
A writer with the enable-submanifests setting off does not create a delta manifest against a tree baseline.
A tree manifest's R card is computed over the walked enumeration, and a delta over a tree baseline's over the composed enumeration.

The partition predicate is the count of leading zero bits of the SHA3-256 digest of the decoded filename, tested against k for leaves and (h+1)*k at height h; content, permission and old name never influence the partition.

The construction is deterministic: leaves carry their group's F cards and a Z card, interiors one S card per member and a Z card, each S card names its child under the repository hash policy, and two writers produce byte-identical artifacts for the same check-in and k.
A scan yielding fewer than two groups emits a flat manifest and no sub-manifest: N = 0, N = 1, at most MAX names with no qualifying boundary, and a boundary suppressed by MIN.
A group holding MAX members forces a boundary whatever the predicate says.
A final group shorter than MIN merges into its predecessor when the two fit in MAX, at height 0 and at every interior height.

A scan yielding one group, or as many groups as nodes, ends the construction with the manifest carrying that height's nodes; otherwise interior sub-manifests form the next height, never a node of height 16.
S card filenames and a leaf's filename and old-name tokens take the canonical encoding: exactly space, newline and backslash escaped, every other byte raw.
Sub-manifests are stored before the manifest that references them, and an unchanged subtree is shared by content addressing.
A supporting server answers reqconfig /config, the scalar marker, with submanifest-k, enable-submanifests and submanifest-auto-retune when the requester holds Read permission.

A receiver validates the adopted state and applies all three settings or none: an invalid value, or enable-submanifests on without a submanifest-k from 1 to 12, leaves the repository's values unchanged, and card order does not affect the result.
A client supporting this specification requests the three settings with reqconfig /config in the clone's cleanup round, after clone authorization succeeds, and a pull does not request them.
A newly cloned repository that could not retrieve the settings leaves enable-submanifests false.
The writer takes k from the stored pin, never derives it per commit, and supports every value from 1 to 12.
A stored k outside 1 to 12 makes the writer fall back to flat manifests rather than substitute a value, and report it.

Automatic selection costs every k from 1 to 12 over the current check-in's entries under the sha3 policy, C(k) = S + sum(L*L)/sum(L), choosing the least cost and the lowest k on a tie; with no candidate it has no result. With no checkout the current check-in is the newest leaf of the main branch. The snapshot choice k_s is refined by replaying the last 200 check-ins under k_s - 1, k_s and k_s + 1, as zit refines it.
A re-tune is forward-only and operator-initiated: the next commit is built under the new value, sharing exactly the byte-identical sub-manifests, and no history is rewritten.
A writer re-tunes automatically only while submanifest-auto-retune is true (default false), and only when a distinct candidate costs less than (1 - m) times the pin's cost; m is 15%, as zit's.
Storing a structural artifact whose S references are absent creates a phantom for each, with the referencing artifact's privacy.
Dephantomizing a sub-manifest retries the deferred processing of every recorded dependent.

A sender refuses to transmit a SUBMANIFEST artifact, or a manifest carrying an S card, to a peer that has not sent pragma send-submanifests, whatever version it announces, with an explicit error and never by converting, downgrading or silently omitting it; a server decides from the request it answers, a client from the replies of its session.
A server whose enable-submanifests setting is false sends pragma avoid-submanifests in every reply, clone replies included, in the leading pragma run after server-version.

A client that received avoid-submanifests emits no S card in a commit created during that session; a commit created outside a session follows the client's own setting, and the pragma does not gate receipt.
column4: covered internally only for the in-session commit: the internal sync session reports the pragma (SyncResult.AvoidSubmanifests) and manifest.Checkin honours it (CheckinOpts.AvoidSubmanifests); the public API commits only outside a session

column3: A peer that reads sub-manifests sends pragma send-submanifests: a client in every request, right after client-version, and a server in every reply, clone replies included, right after server-version, whatever the enable-submanifests setting and the avoid-submanifests pragma; the version it announces is the fossil release whose protocol it speaks.
Crosslinking a tree manifest uses its full enumeration wherever a flat manifest's F cards are used, and an absent sub-manifest defers it as an absent baseline defers a delta.
A SUBMANIFEST artifact has no crosslink effect of its own, and a derived view over an incomplete tree closure is not presented as complete.
A writer emits no S card unless the enable-submanifests setting is true, which is false by default.
When the first S-bearing artifact is stored, a seen-submanifest indicator is recorded.

A local request to enable emission keeps a valid pin and refuses a different explicit k; a stored k outside 1 to 12 refuses a request without an explicit k, naming the stored value, and is replaced by an explicit k from 1 to 12; with no stored k it pins an explicit k from 1 to 12, refuses one outside, or selects one automatically; a request that cannot be met changes neither setting.
Disabling the setting stops new tree manifests and leaves existing ones in place.
SUBMANIFEST is determined by the post-pass reassignment, not while cards are read, and required-card logic treats it as an exception to the D card.
A sweep that discovers crosslink work by the absence of derived rows excludes SUBMANIFEST artifacts or records a completion marker for them, so it never reselects them.
Every consumer of a check-in's file set (checkout, diff, crosslink, rebuild, annotate, commit) obtains it through one shared enumeration interface.
When a tree manifest's processing is deferred, enough is recorded to rediscover it when the missing sub-manifest arrives, and the dephantomization path traverses that record.
The tree walk enforces the depth bound and the repeated-artifact check, and bounds the total sub-manifests visited per enumeration.
column4: the visit bound (2^20) is asserted by construction, not by a case that reaches it

column3: The Appendix A.2 and A.3 artifacts parse, determine their types, recompute their names, walk to the four-file enumeration, and the R card verifies over it.
The Appendix A.4 artifacts parse, recompute their names, walk to the nine-file enumeration, and the R card verifies over it.

The authored Appendix A.5 acceptance vectors (three-level tree, height-0 merge, canonical encoding, delta over a tree) parse, walk, and verify their R cards; the reader accepts them at any partition parameter.

The writer vectors of A.5: the A.4 set reproduced at k = 3, the height-0 merge and three-level vectors reproduced, flat output for N = 1 and a MIN-suppressed boundary, no selection over one name with a first enable failing atomically, and an injected persistence failure leaving no setting applied.
